title: Prehistoric Europe (c. 3000–1000 BCE)
body: Neolithic Revolution, Bronze Age, Iron Age; Megalithic structures (Stonehenge)

title: Ancient Near East & Egypt (c. 3000–500 BCE)
body: Mesopotamian civilizations (Sumer, Babylon, Assyria); Ancient Egypt; Hebrew civilization

title: Classical Greece (c. 800–146 BCE)
body: Archaic Period, Classical Age; Persian Wars, Golden Age of Athens; Alexander the Great & Hellenistic Period

title: Socrates
body: c. 470–399 BCE | Ancient Greece | Philosopher | Father of Western philosophy; Socratic method; martyr for free inquiry.

title: Plato
body: c. 428–348 BCE | Ancient Greece | Philosopher | Founded the Academy; The Republic; theory of Forms; influenced all Western thought.

title: Aristotle
body: 384–322 BCE | Ancient Greece | Philosopher, Scientist | Systematized logic, ethics, politics, biology; tutor to Alexander the Great.

title: Alexander the Great
body: 356–323 BCE | Macedon | Conqueror, King | Spread Hellenistic culture across three continents; reshaped the ancient world.

title: Roman Civilization (c. 753 BCE – 476 CE)
body: Roman Republic (509–27 BCE); Roman Empire (27 BCE – 476 CE); Pax Romana, spread of Christianity

title: Cicero
body: 106–43 BCE | Roman Republic | Orator, Philosopher, Statesman | Greatest Roman orator; defended Republic; philosophical works shaped Western thought

title: Julius Caesar
body: 100–44 BCE | Roman Republic | General, Statesman | Ended the Republic; paved way for Roman Empire; Julian calendar.

title: Augustus Caesar
body: 63 BCE – 14 CE | Roman Empire | First Roman Emperor | Established the Principate; Pax Romana; transformed Rome into an empire.

title: Jesus of Nazareth
body: c. 4 BCE – 30/33 CE | Roman Judea | Religious Teacher | Central figure of Christianity; profoundly shaped Western ethics, art, and culture.

title: Constantine the Great
body: c. 272–337 CE | Roman Empire | Emperor | Legalized Christianity (Edict of Milan); founded Constantinople; shifted empire eastward.

title: Early Middle Ages (c. 500–1000)
body: Fall of Western Roman Empire (476); Migration Period, rise of Islam; Carolingian Empire, Charlemagne; Feudalism, manorialism

title: Charlemagne
body: 742–814 | Frankish Empire | King of the Franks, Emperor | Unified much of Western Europe; Carolingian Renaissance; Father of Europe.

title: High Middle Ages (c. 1000–1300)
body: Agricultural revolution, population growth; Crusades (1095–1291); Rise of universities, Gothic architecture; Magna Carta (1215)

title: William the Conqueror
body: c. 1028–1087 | Normandy/England | King of England | Norman Conquest (1066); transformed English language, law, and society.

title: Thomas Aquinas
body: 1225–1274 | Italy | Theologian, Philosopher | Synthesized Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology; Summa Theologica.

title: Late Middle Ages (c. 1300–1500)
body: Black Death (1347–1351); Hundred Years' War (1337–1453); Crisis of feudalism, rise of nation-states; Late Medieval scholasticism

title: Joan of Arc
body: c. 1412–1431 | France | Military Leader, National Symbol | Turned tide of Hundred Years' War; symbol of French nationalism and faith.

title: Johannes Gutenberg
body: c. 1400–1468 | Germany | Inventor | Movable-type printing press; revolutionized dissemination of knowledge.

title: Renaissance (c. 1300–1600)
body: Italian Renaissance, Humanism; Artistic & intellectual revival; Printing press (Gutenberg, c. 1440)

title: Age of Discovery (c. 1400–1600)
body: European exploration & colonization; Columbus (1492), circumnavigation; Columbian Exchange

title: Christopher Columbus
body: 1451–1506 | Italy/Spain | Explorer | Opened sustained European contact with the Americas; Columbian Exchange.

title: Reformation & Religious Wars (1517–1648)
body: Protestant Reformation (Luther, 1517); Catholic Counter-Reformation; Wars of Religion, Thirty Years' War (1618–1648)

title: Martin Luther
body: 1483–1546 | Germany | Theologian, Reformer | Sparked Protestant Reformation (1517); challenged papal authority; translated Bible.

title: Scientific Revolution (c. 1540–1700)
body: Copernicus, Galileo, Newton; Empirical method, challenge to authority

title: Nicolaus Copernicus
body: 1473–1543 | Poland | Astronomer | Heliocentric theory; launched the Scientific Revolution.

title: Galileo Galilei
body: 1564–1642 | Italy | Scientist, Astronomer | Telescope observations; championed empirical science; conflict with Church.

title: Isaac Newton
body: 1643–1727 | England | Physicist, Mathematician | Laws of motion, universal gravitation, calculus; Principia Mathematica.

title: Enlightenment (c. 1685–1815)
body: Reason, individualism, skepticism of tradition; Locke, Voltaire, Rousseau, Montesquieu; Encyclopédie, salons

title: John Locke
body: 1632–1704 | England | Philosopher | Liberalism, social contract, natural rights; influenced American & French Revolutions.

title: Voltaire
body: 1694–1778 | France | Writer, Philosopher | Enlightenment advocate; championed free speech, religious tolerance, reason.

title: Immanuel Kant
body: 1724–1804 | Germany | Philosopher | Critical philosophy; ethics of duty; synthesized rationalism and empiricism.

title: Age of Revolution (1775–1848)
body: American Revolution (1775–1783); French Revolution (1789–1799); Napoleonic Wars (1803–1815); Latin American independence

title: George Washington
body: 1732–1799 | United States | Military Leader, First President | Led American Revolution; established democratic precedents.

title: Napoleon Bonaparte
body: 1769–1821 | France | Military Commander, Emperor | Spread revolutionary ideals; Napoleonic Code; reshaped European borders.

title: Industrial Revolution (c. 1760–1914)
body: Mechanization, factories, urbanization; Steam engine, railways; Capitalism, class struggle

title: Karl Marx
body: 1818–1883 | Germany | Philosopher, Economist | The Communist Manifesto, Das Kapital; foundational to socialist movements.

title: Age of Imperialism (c. 1870–1914)
body: European colonization of Africa & Asia; Scramble for Africa; Global economic integration

title: World War I (1914–1918)
body: Trench warfare, total war; Fall of empires (Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian, Russian, German); Treaty of Versailles

title: Vladimir Lenin
body: 1870–1924 | Russia | Revolutionary, Political Leader | Led Bolshevik Revolution (1917); founded Soviet Union; shaped 20th-century politics.

title: Interwar Period (1919–1939)
body: Great Depression (1929); Rise of totalitarianism (Fascism, Nazism, Stalinism); League of Nations

title: Winston Churchill
body: 1874–1965 | United Kingdom | Statesman, Prime Minister | Led Britain through WWII; powerful orator; symbol of resistance to tyranny.

title: Franklin D. Roosevelt
body: 1882–1945 | United States | President | New Deal; led US through Great Depression and WWII; shaped postwar order.

title: Adolf Hitler
body: 1889–1945 | Germany | Dictator | Led Nazi Germany; orchestrated WWII and Holocaust; cautionary figure of totalitarianism.

title: Albert Einstein
body: 1879–1955 | Germany/USA | Physicist | Theory of relativity; revolutionized physics; icon of scientific genius.

title: World War II (1939–1945)
body: Holocaust, atomic bomb; Allied victory, UN founded; Beginning of Cold War

title: Cold War (1947–1991)
body: US-Soviet bipolar world; Nuclear arms race, proxy wars; Decolonization, Third World; Fall of Berlin Wall (1989), collapse of USSR (1991)

title: Late 20th Century (1945–2000)
body: European integration (EU); Civil Rights movements; Information Age, globalization; End of apartheid

title: 21st Century (2001–Present)
body: War on Terror (post-9/11); Rise of China, multipolar world; Digital revolution, social media; Climate change crisis; COVID-19 pandemic; Resurgence of populism, challenges to democracy
